articles.headline: Iran warns US of severe military escalation amid stalled bilateral negotiations
articles.title: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that Tehran will launch heavy attacks against American forces if the United States resumes hostilities, issuing an ultimatum during an ongoing eight-month conflict. articles.headline: Gunman kills five people during shooting attack in Krakow
articles.title: Gunman kills 5, injures 12 in Poland’s Krakow shooting attack
articles.summary: Five individuals died and over a dozen suffered injuries after an armed perpetrator opened fire randomly from a vehicle in Krakow's Main Square on November 7, 2026. Local police confirmed that law enforcement officers were among the wounded and that the suspect sustained injuries during a police confrontation. Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that an official investigation is currently underway in Poland's second-largest city.
articles.description: The gunman aimed at random people as he drove by the city's Main Square, Krakow police said

articles.headline: Iran executes three men convicted of armed unrest during protests
articles.title: Iran executes three men over armed unrest during January protests
articles.summary: Iranian authorities executed three men on November 8, 2026, after convictions for operating on behalf of Israel and the United States. Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi, and Reza Zanganeh were found guilty by the judiciary of using firearms and explosives, and damaging public property in Karaj during anti-government demonstrations in January. Ten co-defendants received prison terms ranging from five to ten years following the Supreme Court ruling.
articles.description: The executions are the latest in a ‌series Iran has carried out ‌in ⁠recent months over the January ⁠protests, including of people accused of links to Israel and the U.S.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India data shows cash usage remains unchanged
articles.title: 10 years since demonetisation: Cash usage unchanged, fake notes on the rise
articles.summary: Ten years after demonetisation, Reserve Bank of India data indicates that the policy had minimal impact on reducing overall cash in circulation while counterfeit note detections rose, particularly for 500 rupee notes. Meanwhile, Unified Payments Interface transaction values have experienced steady year-over-year growth relative to India Gross Domestic Product according to the official figures.
articles.description: This Deepavali marks 10 years since Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced overnight demonetisation of 86% of the country’s cash. Data shows some stated aims of the move remain largely unmet

articles.headline: Three dead bodies found inside home of Krakow mass-shooting suspect
articles.title: Two women, man found dead in Krakow mass-shooting suspect’s home, says Prime Minister
articles.summary: Three bodies, including two women and one man, were discovered inside the home of the suspect behind a mass shooting in Krakow, according to Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The victims are likely close family members of the gunman. The attack in Main Square left six people dead and 15 others injured before police shot and wounded the attacker.
articles.description: A Polish man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow on Saturday, November 7, and opened fire, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him, authorities said

articles.headline: Drone attack on military base in northern Colombia kills three soldiers
articles.title: Drone attack on Colombian army base kills three soldiers and wounds 16
articles.summary: A drone strike on a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur killed three soldiers and wounded 16 others, according to the armed forces. President Abelardo de la Espriella condemned the attack on November 7, 2026, attributing the rising rural violence to territorial disputes involving rebel factions like the Gulf Clan and the National Liberation Army in a gold-rich region.
articles.description: Colombian President de la Espriella says those behind the attack in Santa Rosa del Sur will have ‘nowhere to hide’.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality nears severe category with AQI of 383
articles.title: Delhi wakes up to toxic haze on Diwali, close to 'severe' AQI at 383
articles.summary: Delhi experienced toxic air quality with an Air Quality Index reading of 383 on the morning of Deepavali. Out of 54 monitoring stations, 24 recorded severe air quality, while Jahangirpuri reached the highest AQI at 450. According to the Air Quality Early Warning System, pollution levels are expected to remain severe.
articles.description: Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 450, followed by RK Puram at 448, according to the Sameer app.

articles.headline: Global tech stocks tumble following U.S. midterm election results
articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.summary: Global technology stocks slumped after United States midterm election results raised concerns over tighter regulatory scrutiny for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, 2026, erasing $2.53 trillion in market value. Semiconductor firms bore significant losses, though Indian equities bucked the trend with a strong rally as foreign investors bought shares.
articles.description: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

articles.headline: Twenty five killed in Saudi airstrikes in Yemen
articles.title: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
articles.summary: Media outlets linked to the Houthi movement reported that at least twenty five individuals, including women and children, died following Saudi airstrikes in al-Shariyah. The attack occurred amid resumed major fighting across Yemen between the Houthis and forces supporting the internationally recognised government. The United Nations stated that more than one thousand six hundred people have died since hostilities reignited.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.

articles.headline: US military launches new task force to disrupt Iranian land supply routes
articles.title: US launches task force to disrupt Iran’s land-based supply routes
articles.summary: The United States military’s Central Command established Task Force Iron Gate to prevent Iran from utilizing ground routes and the Caspian Sea to transport advanced weapons and materials. Based in Tampa, Florida, the new unit expands previous naval blockades. Meanwhile, officials reported explosions near the Strait of Hormuz and damaged oil tankers.
articles.description: The operation is to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport weapons and other materials, US says.

articles.headline: Former Paraguay President Santiago Peña charged over bank collapse
articles.title: Paraguay's ousted President charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
articles.summary: Prosecutors in Asuncion charged deposed leader Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain following the collapse of Ueno Bank. Judge Humberto Otazu ordered Mr Peña to be held at a military base during investigations. The bank failure froze millions of accounts, triggering Congress to remove Mr Peña and replace him with Pedro Alliana, while public protests and an upcoming teachers union strike persist.
articles.description: In a farewell message released shortly before he was ousted on Friday (November 6), Mr. Peña expressed hope his departure would spare Paraguay further harm

articles.headline: Republican coalition shatters following historic midterm election defeats
articles.title: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
articles.summary: Republicans are experiencing severe infighting after suffering massive losses in the 2026 midterms, losing control of both congressional chambers and key state legislatures. Party strategists and leaders like Vice-President JD Vance are divided on whether to maintain Make America Great Again populist policies or moderate. President Donald Trump responded by appointing Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff.
articles.description: Republicans can stick with Trumpism or chart a new path, writes BBC Washington correspondent Daniel Bush.

articles.headline: Polish PM calls deadly Krakow shooting an act of ‘terrorism’
articles.title: Polish PM calls deadly Krakow shooting an act of ‘terrorism’
articles.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk describes a deadly shooting in Krakow that killed six people as an act of ‘terrorism’.

articles.headline: Explosions reported in southern Iran as two oil tankers catch fire
articles.title: Explosions heard in areas in southern Iran, Iranian media report
articles.summary: Explosions were reported on November 7, 2026, in southern Iran including Qeshm Island, according to Iranian state television, while the Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Officials did not confirm missile strikes, though U.S. forces recently struck the island, raising regional tensions amid ongoing shipping conflicts.
articles.description: State TV said Iranian ‌officials have not confirmed any missile strikes on the areas, while the semi-official Tasnim news agency cited ‌a source as saying that the explosions heard ‌on ⁠Qeshm Island were not related to missile strikes

articles.headline: U.S. military disables cargo vessel attempting to break blockade
articles.title: U.S. military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman
articles.summary: An American military aircraft fired precision munitions and disabled a St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel on November 7, 2026, after it tried to leave regional waters following an Iranian port visit, the U.S. Central Command stated. The command also launched a task force to target advanced weapon smuggling, estimating its naval blockade has blocked over $25 billion in crude oil exports.
articles.description: The St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel tried to ‌depart regional waters after visiting ‌an ⁠Iranian port, and a U.S. plane fired precision munitions at its stern after U.S. forces ​directed the crew to ‌abandon targeted spaces, Central Command said

articles.headline: New Zealand voters reject major political parties amid a deepening economic crisis
articles.title: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
articles.summary: Voters across New Zealand participated in a general election on Saturday amid widespread public dissatisfaction and record low confidence in the political system. Citizens face soaring living costs, high unemployment, and severe healthcare strains, driving a massive exodus of residents abroad while minor political parties made unprecedented electoral gains.
articles.description: The national mood is low, and faith in politics even lower - with voters deserting the major parties at the polls.

articles.headline: Police clash with protesters as anti-government rallies sweep France
articles.title: Police clash with protesters as anti-government rallies sweep France
articles.description: Police have clashed with protesters in Paris as Yellow Vests defied a ban on their rally, leading to arrests.

articles.headline: Defence minister Rajnath Singh calls for highest military preparedness at Bagdogra Air Force station
articles.title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
articles.summary: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged armed forces personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force station in West Bengal to maintain high operational readiness amid an increasingly complex security landscape. Speaking near the frontier with China, Singh highlighted emerging threats including cyber attacks, proxy wars, and misinformation campaigns, while reaffirming the government's push for indigenous defence technologies through start-ups.
articles.description: Addressing personnel at key airbase near China frontier, Defence Minister warns of adversaries exploiting ‘vulnerabilities’; he also reviews Army’s LAC infrastructure, operational preparedness and lauds initiatives aimed at strengthening ties with local communities

articles.headline: Thousands of demonstrators protest across France against rising cost of living
articles.title: More than 140,000 rally as new protests against rising costs sweep France
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of protesters rallied across France for a fourth consecutive weekend to demonstrate against the rising cost of living. The Ministry of the Interior reported 146,000 participants nationwide, while unions estimated 250,000 demonstrators. The protests involved heavy security deployments, clashes in Paris and Lyon, and occurred ahead of the presidential election scheduled for April.
articles.description: Tear gas fired in Paris and Lyon as interior minister warns authorities are 'ready and waiting' for rioters and looters.

articles.headline: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia faces threat as Russian drones close in
articles.title: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia faces threat as Russian drones close in
articles.description: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia, once a refuge for those fleeing the war, is now facing growing danger.

articles.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials to discuss ceasefire
articles.title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
articles.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations to the White House to discuss a six-day ceasefire in the Kherson region. The truce allowed for the evacuation of residents from Oleshky. While officials praised the humanitarian progress, some analysts suggest the move was orchestrated by Vladimir Putin to influence US midterm elections.
articles.description: The US first lady was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire.

articles.headline: United States President Donald Trump orders Department of Justice to investigate Democrats
articles.title: Trump orders DOJ to investigate Democrats for ‘threatening’ people
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump directed the Department of Justice to investigate Democratic lawmakers for alleged threats following their midterm election victory. Writing on social media, Trump claimed without evidence that Democratic probes into his administration and associates amounted to criminal extortion. Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the November elections, granting them investigative powers.
articles.description: Trump lashed out at Democrats on Truth Social days after the party won control of Congress.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces report battlefield advances as deadly strikes hit Sanaa
articles.title: Yemeni gov’t forces report advances as Houthis say deadly strikes hit Sanaa
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces reported repelling Houthi assaults and advancing in Marib and al-Jawf provinces during ongoing military operations. Meanwhile, the Houthi-run Saba news agency reported that air strikes killed at least 27 people and wounded about 30 others in al-Shariya village in Sanaa province. The Houthis blamed the Saudi-led coalition, while Al Jazeera could not independently verify the competing claims.
articles.description: Civilians bear the brunt of fighting as 27 people reported killed in strikes on a village in Sanaa province.

articles.headline: US offers twenty million dollars for Iran nuclear details
articles.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
articles.summary: The United States State Department announced a reward of up to twenty million dollars for information regarding Iran's nuclear programme, including facilities, equipment, and associated personnel. Meanwhile, United States Central Command established Task Force Iron Gate to restrict weapons movement and sanctioned material across Iranian borders, while regional mediators continued efforts to negotiate an end to the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospect of renewing strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities.

articles.headline: Houthis report 25 killed in Yemen strikes
articles.title: Houthis report 25 killed in Yemen strikes
articles.description: Yemen’s Houthis say at least 25 people have been killed and 30 injured in air strikes.

articles.headline: Ukraine says Russia intensifies strikes ahead of diplomatic peace talks
articles.title: Ukraine says Russia ramps up strikes to pressure Kyiv at talks
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles on November 7, 2026, causing widespread power outages across five regions. The Energy Ministry reported severe transmission disruptions in Kyiv. Mr. Zelenskyy alleged Moscow aims to exert pressure ahead of U.S.-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11, while the Russian Defence Ministry confirmed strikes on military and energy infrastructure.
articles.description: Ukraine's Energy Ministry said "a massive attack on a number of energy facilities" had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding region

articles.headline: Yemeni Houthis launch drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi sites
articles.title: Saudi oil sites, troops and Riyadh airport targeted: Houthis
articles.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement carried out six military operations on November 7, 2026, targeting Saudi troops and infrastructure. According to military spokesperson Yahya Saree, the strikes hit Aramco oil facilities, Riyadh airport, and military installations on both sides of the border amid an ongoing conflict involving a Saudi-led coalition.
articles.description: The Iran-backed group, which is fighting a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government, allegedly launched six operations

articles.headline: Israel builds 90km network of military roads across southern Lebanon
articles.title: Israel builds 90km network of military roads across southern Lebanon
articles.description: Israel is building roads and military outposts across southern Lebanon.

articles.headline: World Bank brief highlights extreme poverty decline and high prosperity gap
articles.title: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
articles.summary: According to a World Bank brief, India experienced a significant decline in extreme poverty between 2011 and 2023, with hundreds of millions moving out of poverty. However, the report highlights a high prosperity gap driven by flat real earnings, low-productivity work, and rising youth unemployment, indicating that many individuals require substantial income increases to reach prosperity.
articles.description: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

articles.headline: Five killed and at least 10 injured in Krakow shooting
articles.title: Five killed and at least 10 injured in Krakow shooting
articles.description: Five people have been killed and at least 10 injured in a shooting near the main market square in Krakow, Poland.

articles.headline: New Zealand general election ends without clear winner as major parties prepare for talks
articles.title: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
articles.summary: New Zealand faced political uncertainty following a tight general election where Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party won forty-two seats and the Labour Party secured thirty-six. With neither major party achieving a majority, smaller groups like the Opportunity Party emerged as potential kingmakers. According to polling experts, cost of living pressures heavily influenced voter sentiment during the contest.
articles.description: Weeks of coalition talks could follow after preliminary results pointed to a highly divided national parliament.

articles.headline: Allahabad High Court criticises Uttar Pradesh Police over routine violations of fundamental rights
articles.title: Allahabad High Court slams U.P. Police over routine violations of fundamental rights
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court strongly criticised the Uttar Pradesh Police for routine infringements on civil liberties while ordering the release of a petitioner who was allegedly detained unlawfully. Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev rejected the state's excuse regarding a malfunctioning CCTV system caused by a thunderstorm, noting that footage appeared to be deliberately withheld. The court also ordered the state to pay twenty thousand rupees in litigation costs.
articles.description: Ordering the release of a petitioner whose family alleged that he was forcibly picked up by police in plain clothes on September 5, the Bench says police appear to have little regard for constitutional freedoms

articles.headline: Five people killed in shooting near Krakow market square in Poland
articles.title: At least six people killed in shooting in Poland’s Krakow
articles.summary: Five people were killed and about a dozen others wounded during a shooting incident near the main market square in Krakow, Poland. Police stated that a gunman fired at random people from a vehicle before being neutralised by officers and transported to hospital. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk addressed the attack on social media, confirming that authorities were actively investigating the circumstances surrounding the tragic event.
articles.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk says police are investigating after 'tragic shooting' in second-largest city.

articles.headline: Airstrikes in al-Shariya village near Sanaa kill twenty-two people
articles.title: Airstrike kills 22 people near Yemen's capital, Houthi official says
articles.summary: Attacks hit several homes in al-Shariya village near the Yemeni capital of Sanaa on November 7, 2026, resulting in twenty-two deaths and thirty injuries, mostly among women and children, according to Anees Alasbahi, a spokesman for the Houthi-run Health Ministry. Alasbahi attributed the assault to Saudi Arabia, though the claim remained unverified and the Saudi Information Ministry did not immediately respond. The incident follows a November 6 market strike in southern Yemen that killed at least thirty people amid escalating conflict between the Iranian-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed forces.
articles.description: Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of November 7 strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital

articles.headline: Russian drone and missile attacks escalate across Zaporizhzhia region
articles.title: ‘They started bombing us with drones’: Russian attacks unnerve Zaporizhzhia
articles.summary: Escalating Russian drone and missile strikes have forced residents from villages like Preobrazhenka into shelters in the Ukrainian regional capital of Zaporizhzhia. The attacks include a November 2 strike in Komyshuvakha that killed at least fifty people, alongside recent hits on bridges, shopping malls, and buses. Regional military administration official Denys Knysh stated that authorities are prepared to evacuate the city if security conditions deteriorate further, while displaced residents and local workers express fear and uncertainty regarding the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: A region once offering refuge becomes increasingly dangerous, as 50 people are killed in a single attack.

articles.headline: Gaza displacement camps collapse under rainwater
articles.title: Gaza displacement camps collapse under rainwater
articles.description: Rainwater is inundating displacement camps across Gaza as makeshift shelters collapse. Al Jazeera’s Nour Khaled reports.

articles.headline: Heavy rain floods Gaza camps and damages unsafe buildings
articles.title: Buildings damaged in Israeli bombings risk collapse as rain inundates Gaza
articles.summary: Severe storms and heavy rain on November 7, 2026, flooded displacement camps and damaged structures across the Gaza Strip, leaving thousands of displaced Palestinians shivering in soaked shelters. Water levels rose by thirty to forty centimetres in multiple camps, including al-Mina, while damaged buildings in Nuseirat faced collapse risks. Officials from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs and the Gaza Municipality reported severe shortages of shelter supplies, fuel, and equipment to handle the widespread flooding and structural dangers.
articles.description: Floods have swept through Gaza after heavy rain, endangering families and putting war-damaged buildings at risk.

articles.headline: Heavy rains flood displacement camps across Gaza
articles.title: Heavy rains flood displacement camps across Gaza
articles.description: Heavy rains and strong winds have flooded and damaged displacement tents across Gaza.

articles.headline: Russian drone and missile strikes cause widespread blackouts across Ukraine
articles.title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that overnight Russian missile and drone attacks damaged energy infrastructure across 12 Ukrainian regions, leaving the capital Kyiv facing severe power, water, and heating disruptions. The bombardment involved over 30 ballistic missiles and 170 drones, injuring nine people. These strikes occurred ahead of upcoming trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi and followed a recent humanitarian evacuation in Oleshky.
articles.description: The attacks come before Ukrainian and Russian delegations are due to take part in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

articles.headline: New report reveals artificial intelligence is accelerating Anthropic research development
articles.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
articles.summary: A report published Thursday by the artificial intelligence safety research organization METR revealed that Anthropic models are improving twice as fast as last year largely due to artificial intelligence assistance. The findings highlight significant productivity gains among employees using unreleased internal models. However, researchers noted that Anthropic heavily redacted the public report to protect sensitive competitive information from rivals.
articles.description: Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company's models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down. That's according to a new report published Thursday by the AI safety research organization METR, following an 11-week investigation […]

articles.headline: Tankers carrying Russian diesel change course amid ongoing US trader hesitation
articles.title: Why are oil traders refusing to buy Russian diesel after Trump-Putin deal?
articles.summary: At least three tankers carrying Russian diesel have altered their destinations away from the United States following a temporary sanctions exemption agreed between President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in October. Traders remain hesitant to purchase the fuel due to continued congressional bans and legal risks. While Moscow insists the trade will proceed, experts state the initial shipments will provide minimal relief to high American fuel prices.
articles.description: Zero Russian diesel has reached the US as tankers divert and buyers fear legal action.

articles.headline: Dozens killed in Yemen market strike as government offensive against Houthis continues
articles.title: Dozens killed as humanitarian crisis mounts in Yemen: What next for war?
articles.summary: A missile strike killed dozens of people at a market in the Taiz governorate on Friday, with Yemen's internationally recognized government and the Houthi movement blaming each other for the attack. The violence coincides with an ongoing month-long military offensive launched by the Presidential Leadership Council to reclaim territory. The protracted conflict has displaced hundreds of thousands of people and deepened a severe humanitarian crisis across the nation.
articles.description: Government forces reclaim key territories in Taiz and Lahij but face setbacks under Houthi resistance in certain areas.

articles.headline: Winter storm floods tens of thousands of displaced families' tents in Gaza
articles.title: Rains flood 70,000 displaced families’ tents in Gaza
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall from the first winter storm of the season flooded approximately 70,000 tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the Gaza Strip within 12 hours. According to Gaza's Government Media Office, the disaster caused initial losses estimated at three million dollars, collapsed walls, and triggered about 1,500 distress calls. Officials blamed Israeli restrictions on shelter materials for blocking reconstruction efforts.
articles.description: Initial losses are estimated at about $3m, according to Gaza's Government Media Office.

articles.headline: New Zealand election remains too close to call
articles.title: New Zealand vote still too close to call as results trickle in
articles.summary: New Zealand's general election on November 7, 2026, remained tightly contested as early vote counts showed Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party and the opposition Labour Party neck-and-neck. With neither party projected to win an outright majority, attention turned to minor factions like the centrist Opportunity Party. Voters faced rising living costs and economic pressures driven by global fuel shocks.
articles.description: New Zealand’s election remained too close to call on November 7, as early results trickled in from across the country, with neither the governing National-Luxon coalition nor Labour falling short of a majority and minor parties weighing in, including a rising Opportunity Party

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi discusses new memoir and political history in interview
articles.title: Sonia Gandhi interview: ‘Great damage done to the fabric of India by BJP’
articles.summary: In an interview with The Hindu regarding her forthcoming book Belonging: A Journey of Love published by HarperCollins India, senior Indian National Congress politician Sonia Gandhi answered questions from N. Ram about her life, the Emergency, and Indian politics. Gandhi reflected on her decades in India, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi and Indira Gandhi, and her decision to author her own story.
articles.description: Ahead of the launch of her book, Sonia Gandhi speaks to The Hindu, answering a number of questions — personal and political

articles.headline: Sudan child malnutrition crisis deepens amid civil war and drought
articles.title: Sudan war and climate change see parents struggle to feed their children
articles.summary: Severe acute malnutrition is threatening hundreds of thousands of young children across Sudan due to ongoing civil war, displacement, and drought. Medical personnel at facilities like Port Sudan Teaching Hospital report extreme overcrowding and financial strains. According to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, hundreds of thousands of children under five are expected to suffer from severe acute malnutrition in 2026, while conflict zones like Darfur and Blue Nile State face worsening humanitarian conditions and inadequate aid.
articles.description: War, poverty and climate change are all affecting Sudanese, with increasing cases of child malnutrition.

articles.headline: State security forces restrict access to proposed Siang dam site
articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.summary: Central security forces and State police have deployed barricades and concertina wires near Parong village in Arunachal Pradesh to restrict unauthorized access to the Siang river. Parong in Siang district is one of three proposed locations identified for a Pre-Feasibility Report regarding the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project developed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation.
articles.description: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

articles.headline: Trump appoints Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff
articles.title: Who is Stephen Miller, Trump’s new Chief of Staff?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller as his new Chief of Staff on November 6, 2026. Miller, 41, replaces Susie Wiles following a Republican defeat in the midterms. Known for his hardline immigration policies and mass deportation plans, Miller's appointment drew praise from the Make America Great Again movement but severe condemnation from Democratic leaders including Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.
articles.description: Stephen Miller, one of U.S. President Donald Trump’s closest aides for decades, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week

articles.headline: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigns amid violent banking protests
articles.title: After Donald Trump’s midterm poll rout, South America breathes easy as far-right feels the heat
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of protesters flooded the streets of Asuncion on November 4, 2026, after being locked out of their accounts at the countrys largest bank, prompting President Santiago Pena to resign. As Congress moved to impeach him, Senator Antonio Velazquez stated on November 5 that Pena had disappeared and likely fled to Argentina to seek asylum following the unrest.
articles.description: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

articles.headline: US president Donald Trump weighs military options amid escalating tensions with Iran
articles.title: Will Trump strike nuclear sites again as Iran engages ‘cognitive warfare’?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump is facing political pressure and mixed diplomatic signals regarding the conflict with Iran following midterms. According to media reports, United States forces conducted minor strikes on Qeshm Island while Iranian health officials distributed iodine tablets near nuclear facilities. Observers note that leadership in Washington is evaluating potential military actions and upcoming decisions before January.
articles.description: The US president has been sending mixed messages after his party suffered a defeat at the midterm elections.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV delivers homily to thousands in Uruguay
articles.title: Pope Leo XIV delivers homily to thousands in Uruguay
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV delivers homily to thousands in Uruguay

articles.headline: Democrats capture full control of U.S. Congress in midterms
articles.title: U.S. midterm election results: Senate, House and Governor shifts before and after
articles.summary: The November 2026 U.S. midterm elections resulted in a dramatic shift as Democrats secured majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, crossing the 218-seat threshold in the lower chamber. Driven by voter discontent over economic pressures and living costs, the results contrasted sharply with the 2022 midterms. Several candidates achieved historic firsts, including Abdul El-Sayed entering the Senate as the first Muslim member.
articles.description: Democrats surged to full control of Congress in the November 2026 U.S. midterm elections, flipping the Senate and House after winning net seats across key battlegrounds and sweeping into Republican strongholds. Here’s what changed between 2022 and 2026 midterms.

articles.headline: Apple accelerates Siri AI roadmap to match industry rivals
articles.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
articles.summary: According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple Chief Executive Officer John Ternus is urging artificial intelligence leader Craig Federighi to quicken development on a powerful virtual assistant. Upcoming software updates will introduce fine-grained control over first-party applications and third-party integrations. Furthermore, the company aims to develop autonomous capabilities allowing the assistant to track goals and handle ongoing multi-step tasks by next year.
articles.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI's Dots or Meta's Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it's […]

articles.headline: Manchester United secure dramatic draw against Aston Villa
articles.title: Man United earn 4-4 draw against Aston Villa but remain in relegation zone
articles.summary: Manchester United secured a four-all draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday after scoring two stoppage-time goals. Despite the late comeback, the Premier League club remains in eighteenth place with eight points from ten matches under manager Michael Carrick. In other league fixtures, Chelsea suffered a defeat against Sunderland while Liverpool defeated Crystal Palace three to one.
articles.description: Michael Carrick's team continue forgettable season with last-gasp draw at Old Trafford in front of angry home fans.

articles.headline: Nineteen stranded Indian seafarers evacuated safely from Yemen
articles.title: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen evacuated, Embassy says
articles.summary: Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Hodeidah and Sana'a for two weeks were successfully evacuated and are returning home, according to an announcement by the Indian Embassy in Yemen on November 8, 2026. The diplomatic mission expressed gratitude for assistance in facilitating their departure. This follows a separate incident involving fourteen Indian nationals aboard a yacht near the Yemeni coast amid regional military escalations.
articles.description: The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe

articles.headline: Qatari PM says US willing to seek solution to war with Iran
articles.title: Qatari PM says US willing to seek solution to war with Iran
articles.description: Qatari PM says US willing to seek solution to war with Iran

articles.headline: U.S. and China officials hold trade talks ahead of APEC summit
articles.title: Top U.S., China officials raise trade 'concerns' as APEC approaches
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a conference call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on November 6, 2026, to discuss bilateral economic commitments ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. While Washington pressed Beijing to immediately implement prior agreements, Beijing voiced concerns over recent American trade restrictions and sanctions.
articles.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and discussed economic and trade commitments over the last year

articles.headline: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Ben Shelton to claim Paris Masters title
articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz beats Ben Shelton to win Paris Masters tennis title
articles.summary: Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz defeated American Ben Shelton 7-6, 7-5 in the Paris Masters final on Sunday. The victory marks his ninth 1000-level title and his fifth tour-level win of the year. Alcaraz triumphed after nearly two hours of play, having previously saved match points against Taylor Fritz in the quarterfinals. Shelton, ranked fourth globally, experienced his first defeat in a Masters final.
articles.description: Alcaraz bagged a 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 straight sets for an elusive Paris crown before the year-end ATP Finals.

articles.headline: Former Keralam Excise Commissioner alleges corruption against senior officials
articles.title: Ex-Keralam Excise Commissioner flags corruption, bribery in report to govt; CPI(M) alleges Minister’s involvement
articles.summary: Former Keralam Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao submitted a report to the State government alleging that two senior officials engaged in bribery and corruption involving bar owners. The report, submitted on November 6, 2026, recommended a Vigilance inquiry and prompted the Communist Party of India Marxist to question Excise Minister M. Liju over potential links.
articles.description: In report submitted to State government shortly before being relieved from the post, Seeram Sambasiva Rao mentions that Excise Minister M. Liju was acquainted with one of the bar owners allegedly involved in the transactions

articles.headline: New Zealand governing National Party leads in early general election results
articles.title: Two main parties neck and neck after New Zealand vote, near complete count
articles.summary: New Zealand's centre-right National Party secured 31.19 percent of the vote in early results, ahead of the opposition Labour Party at 28.35 percent. Polling stations closed following a mixed-member proportional election held on Saturday, with the Electoral Commission aiming to release preliminary outcomes from 95 percent of polling stations by the end of the evening.
articles.description: New Zealand's National and Labour parties secure just short of 30 percent of the popular vote.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality remains very poor as schools shift to hybrid mode
articles.title: Delhi air ‘very poor’ with AQI reading of 364
articles.summary: Delhi recorded a very poor air quality index reading of 364 on November 7, 2026, prompting authorities to implement Stage III measures under the Graded Response Action Plan. In response to the worsening pollution, the Delhi Directorate of Education directed all schools to conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode starting immediately.
articles.description: The Delhi Directorate of Education has directed all government and private schools to conduct classes up to class 5 in hybrid mode in view of worsening air quality in the national capital

articles.headline: Tens of thousands protest in Amsterdam demanding action on Gaza
articles.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing Dutch government on Gaza, Israel
articles.summary: More than 200,000 demonstrators marched through Amsterdam on November 8, 2026, urging the Dutch government to implement stricter trade sanctions, halt arms sales, and formally declare Israel's Gaza campaign as genocide. Organised by groups including Amnesty International, the protest highlighted public discontent over the conflict. Prime Minister Rob Jetten defended his administration's diplomatic efforts, citing ongoing political pressure to alleviate the humanitarian crisis.
articles.description: Organisers of the “Red Line” demonstration called for stricter trade sanctions, a halt to arms sales, and an official declaration that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide

articles.headline: Demonstrators fill Amsterdam streets to protest Israeli military actions
articles.title: Hundreds of thousands join Amsterdam’s ‘Red Line’ protest against Israel
articles.summary: Thousands of individuals gathered in Amsterdam on Sunday for a Red Line demonstration, demanding that authorities enforce stricter trade restrictions on Israel and halt arms sales. Amnesty International reported that over 200,000 participants joined the march. Protesters criticized the Dutch government for perceived inaction regarding the conflict in Gaza, which has resulted in at least 74,000 Palestinian deaths since October 2023, according to reports.
articles.description: Protesters seek stricter trade restrictions on Israel and a halt to all arms sales.

articles.headline: Democrats plan congressional probes targeting Elon Musk and Stephen Miller
articles.title: Democrats eye Musk, Miller probes after midterm rout
articles.summary: Incoming Democratic congressional leaders announced plans on November 8, 2026, to investigate tech billionaire Elon Musk and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller following the party's midterm victories. Representative Robert Garcia stated that upcoming hearings will examine Mr. Musk's involvement in federal layoffs and Mr. Miller's hardline immigration policies. Meanwhile, Democratic leaders also expressed support for initiating impeachment proceedings against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
articles.description: California Representative Robert Garcia ‌said investigations will focus on Musk's involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency's firing of federal workers last year, and Miller's role in Trump's ‌hardline immigration crackdown

articles.headline: Elvis and Eminem rights holders file lawsuits against AI music firm Suno
articles.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
articles.summary: Representatives for Elvis Presley's estate and publishers of Eminem's music filed lawsuits against artificial intelligence firm Suno. The legal complaints allege that the company unlawfully generates soundalikes and lyrics mimicking iconic performers. Lawyers representing the Presley estate claim violations of Tennessee's ELVIS Act. Suno spokesperson Cat McCormack stated that the platform prohibits unauthorized artist replications and utilizes screening tools to prevent misuse.
articles.description: Suno is facing yet another pair of lawsuits. A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The lawyers in the Presley suit claim that Suno has violated Tennessee's […]

articles.headline: Israeli President Isaac Herzog faces key choice on government formation
articles.title: President Herzog faces key choice as Israel struggles to form government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog must select a politician to form a new government following an inconclusive election where neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a parliamentary majority. Although Eisenkot received sixty-seven endorsements from lawmakers, forming a stable coalition remains challenging due to mutual vetoes, uncooperative ultra-Orthodox parties, and ongoing disputes involving Arab-led factions.
articles.description: Eisenkot's bloc and Arab-led parties seek to oust Netanyahu, but failure to form government could leave him in power.

articles.headline: United States military offers reward for information on Iran nuclear program
articles.title: United States offers $20 million reward for information on 'Iran's nuclear program': CENTCOM
articles.summary: The United States Central Command announced a financial reward of up to twenty million dollars through the Rewards for Justice program for details regarding Iran's nuclear facilities, equipment, and personnel. While President Donald Trump stated that Tehran is eager to negotiate an end to the ongoing conflict, the State Department cited persistent noncompliance with International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards as justification.
articles.description: U.S. State Department program, Rewards for Justice, gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward

articles.headline: Russian missile attack on Kyiv injures residents and damages buildings
articles.title: Russia launches missile attack on Kyiv, injuring residents
articles.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck residential and kindergarten buildings in Kyiv, injuring two individuals according to city officials and Mayor Vitali Klitschko. The assault followed warnings from President Volodymyr Zelenskyy regarding escalating threats to Ukrainian infrastructure, occurring simultaneously as diplomatic delegations prepare for upcoming United States-led negotiations in Abu Dhabi.
articles.description: Air strikes damage buildings and injure two civilians after Zelenskyy warns of potential for new attacks.

articles.headline: Supreme Court identifies vehicular emissions as major contributor to Delhi air pollution
articles.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated on November 6, 2026, that vehicular emissions heavily drive air pollution in the Delhi-National Capital Region as the air quality index approached the severe category at 391. During a hearing led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati outlined measures across five sectors, while the bench scheduled further review for November 16.
articles.description: The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad

articles.headline: Indian youth movement demands political accountability and fair elections
articles.title: India’s ‘cockroach’ movement seeks to restore culture of accountability
articles.summary: Founded by Abhijeet Dipke, the Cockroach Janta Party mobilized thousands in May to protest exam leaks, unemployment, and living costs, leading to the education minister's resignation. Protesters now target the chief election commissioner, accusing the election body of voter list manipulation favoring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party, which denies the allegations and accuses demonstrators of undermining democracy.
articles.description: India's Cockroach Janta Party is a youth movement demanding political accountability, employment and fair elections.

articles.headline: Israeli authorities release Palestinian journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh after five days
articles.title: Israeli forces release Palestinian journalist Abou Shhadeh
articles.summary: Israeli authorities released Palestinian journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh without charge after a five-day detention at a Shin Bet facility in Petah Tikva. Defence team members from the legal rights group Adalah stated that the arrest aimed to intimidate Arab society and delegitimise Palestinian votes, noting police lacked evidence for suspicions regarding foreign contact.
articles.description: Abed Abou Shhadeh says his detention was part of Israel's political measures 'to intimidate Arab society as a whole'.
