articles.headline: Indonesian tennis player Janice Tjen advances to Chennai Open semifinals
articles.title: Janice Tjen’s success is forging a new path for tennis in badminton mad Indonesia
articles.summary: Indonesian tennis player Janice Tjen advanced to the semifinals of the Chennai Open on November 6, 2026, by defeating Polina Kudermetova. Ranked 75th, Tjen has experienced a breakthrough season, rising from outside the top 400 at the start of 2025 to a career-high ranking of 35 in August, while also ending a 22-year Grand Slam win drought for Indonesian women at the US Open.

articles.headline: US midterm outcomes prompt Israeli anxiety over future bilateral strategic ties
articles.title: US midterm results spark fears in Israel over future of two countries' ties
articles.summary: US midterm election results have triggered widespread concern across Israel regarding the durability of the bilateral alliance and future military aid. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced criticism from political opponents as analysts questioned how shifting congressional power and President Donald Trump recent statements might impact defense funding, arms sales, and joint military projects at a sensitive time for domestic Israeli politics.
articles.description: Staunch US support of Israel has been raised as one of the reasons why Republicans performed so badly.

articles.headline: Magnitude-6.1 earthquake strikes off Tokyo coast without triggering tsunami alerts
articles.title: Magnitude-6.1 earthquake hits off Tokyo, no tsunami alert: weather agency
articles.summary: A magnitude-6.1 earthquake struck off the coast of Tokyo on Friday, according to Japanese authorities. The shallow tremor hit at 7.39 p.m. in the Kanto region with its epicentre located 169 kilometres southeast of Asahi. The Japan Meteorological Agency recorded a seismic intensity of 3, though no immediate reports of damage, injuries or tsunami alerts emerged from the event.
articles.description: There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football after glittering career
articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal’s polarising icon and his bitter final act
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has ended his international career with Portugal after making a record 234 appearances and scoring 146 goals. The 41-year-old forward announced his retirement in a video statement following a tense final campaign that concluded at the FIFA World Cup 2026. He leaves the national team holding numerous scoring records despite never winning a world championship title.
articles.description: After announcing his international retirement, Portugal's longstanding captain leaves behind a complicated legacy.

articles.headline: Congress urges voters to defeat BJP over rising rural inflation
articles.title: Congress says people must express outrage over inflation by teaching BJP a lesson in upcoming polls
articles.summary: Opposition leaders criticized federal policies by pointing to survey findings indicating that rural households allocate over half their monthly earnings toward basic food purchases. The political party argued that citizens face continuous financial pressure from mounting debt and elevated borrowing costs, calling upon regional electorates to register their discontent by opposing the ruling administration during upcoming legislative contests across multiple states.
articles.description: Under the Modi Government, the common person’s life had become trapped in a dual vicious cycle of inflation and debt, Jairam Ramesh shared on X

articles.headline: Russian extremist group Male State denies involvement in European bomb threats
articles.title: Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats
articles.summary: The Male State group has denied responsibility for hoax bomb threats disrupting European aviation and Irish media on Friday. Messages on Telegram mocked the allegations, while Italian defence minister Guido Crosetto warned of a hybrid strategy to increase chaos. The original hoax email was sent to Rome airport officials on Thursday, prompting flight diversions and security responses across Europe.
articles.description: Scores of flights across Europe have received bomb threats this week, but no explosives have been found so far.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues notice to KPCC office-bearers over social media post targeting CJI
articles.title: Supreme Court notice to KPCC office-bearers on contempt plea for social media post against CJI
articles.summary: The Supreme Court sought responses from Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee office-bearers on Friday regarding contempt proceedings for a social media post targeting Chief Justice Surya Kant. Justice Aravind Kumar stated that judicial restraint is not an institutional weakness. The disputed post was deleted, and the party president apologized, but the apex court issued a notice to show cause under the Constitution.
articles.description: A post against the CJI from the official X account of the Keralam unit of Congress went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before it was deleted

articles.headline: Gauhati High Court quashes preventive detention of Assam activist Pranab Doley
articles.title: Gauhati High Court quashes Assam activist’s NSA detention
articles.summary: The Gauhati High Court quashed the preventive detention of land rights activist Pranab Doley under the National Security Act on Friday, paving the way for his release after 118 days in custody. Justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund declared the detention illegal. Mr. Doley had been arrested in July after participating in a protest against a luxury hotel project near Kaziranga National Park.
articles.description: The State government invoked the National Security Act against Pranab Doley on July 30, a day after a court granted him bail for protesting a luxury hotel project near Kaziranga National Park

articles.headline: Nithya Raman elected as mayor of Los Angeles
articles.title: ‘City of immigrants’: Who is Nithya Raman, the Los Angeles mayor-elect?
articles.summary: Nithya Raman won the mayoral election in Los Angeles, becoming the first Asian-American to lead the city and the latest democratic socialist to secure a major United States municipality. Born in India and raised in the United States, Raman focused her campaign on expanding affordable housing, combating homelessness, and protecting immigrant communities. According to the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority, the city housed roughly forty-four thousand homeless residents as of 2025. Raman previously defeated incumbent David Ryu in 2019 to join the city council.
articles.description: The two biggest cities in the US will now be led by Indian-origin immigrants - both democratic socialists.

articles.headline: Asian political parties adopt Seoul Declaration against unilateral actions
articles.title: Asian parties reject ‘unilateral actions’, call for respect for international law
articles.summary: The International Conference of Asian Political Parties adopted the Seoul Declaration during its thirteenth General Assembly in Seoul, expressing grave concern regarding unilateral actions and geopolitical rivalries. Representatives from eighty-three political parties across Asia attended the summit, which ran from November 4 to 6, 2026. The participating delegates urged all nations to respect international law consistently while upholding the core principles outlined in the United Nations Charter to maintain regional and global peace.
articles.description: The declaration was unanimously adopted at the 13th General Assembly of ICAPP, held in Seoul from November 4 to 6, with representatives of 83 political parties from across Asia participating

articles.headline: IT ministry approves twelve new electronic component projects
articles.title: IT Ministry approves 12 more projects under ECMS scheme
articles.summary: The government approved twelve new projects under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme, bringing total approved applications to one hundred eighteen and pushing committed investments to seventy-seven thousand fifty-one crore rupees. According to IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, the latest approvals include a copper foil facility by Indo Asia Copper Limited in Amreli, Gujarat. These initiatives aim to deepen domestic manufacturing across the electronics supply chain rather than focusing exclusively on final assembly.
articles.description: The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) allows the government to approve turnover-linked incentives across the component industry.

articles.headline: Supreme Court refuses to suspend Tarun Tejpal's rape sentence
articles.title: Supreme Court refuses to suspend Tarun Tejpal’s 10-year sentence in 2013 rape case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court declined to suspend the 10-year prison sentence of journalist Tarun Tejpal on November 6, 2026. Tejpal was convicted in August by the Bombay High Court for raping a junior colleague in Goa in 2013, overturning a previous acquittal. While his defence argued the case was false, the Goa government opposed the relief and requested an enhanced prison term.
articles.description: A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale said it was ‘not a fit case’ for suspension, while the Goa government’s plea for a longer sentence is pending

articles.headline: Kerala High Court rules political activities have no place in institutions
articles.title: Kerala HC ruling on political activities in campuses, Ambedkar and the right to protest | Explained
articles.summary: A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court quashed an order permitting sixteen Students Federation of India activists to write semester examinations at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit. The suspended students had faced disciplinary action for allegedly staging a mock cremation of Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas and damaging her vehicle. The court cited a 2017 precedent stating that political activities like hunger strikes have no place in academic institutions. The aggrieved students subsequently appealed to the Supreme Court.
articles.description: Division Bench of Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna said educational Institutions are meant for imparting education and not campus politics; by their political ambition, the political parties cannot hold to ransom the educational institution or the right of the civilised students to receive education, the Bench stated

articles.headline: Election Commission allows excluded voters to resubmit enumeration forms
articles.title: Election Commission gives fresh opportunity to electors left out of SIR draft rolls in Delhi, six States
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India issued a directive allowing voters categorized as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate across seven states during the special intensive revision process to resubmit enumeration forms rather than filing Form 6. This decision followed a Supreme Court hearing regarding a petition filed by activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri concerning voter deletions in Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana, and Nagaland. The updated policy ensures voters can retain their historical identification numbers.
articles.description: The directions apply to Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland

articles.headline: Rupee surges 52 points to close at 93.89 against the US dollar
articles.title: Rupee surges 52 points to close at 93.89 against U.S. dollar
articles.summary: The Indian rupee appreciated by 52 paise to close provisionally at 93.89 against the United States dollar on November 6, 2026. The currency gained support from a softer United States dollar, declining crude oil prices, rising domestic equity markets, and positive foreign institutional investor inflows, according to forex traders and analysts.
articles.description: Forex traders said a surge in domestic markets and fears of a slowdown in AI spending also supported the rupee

articles.headline: Keralam mangrove cover increases over past decade according to new study
articles.title: Keralam’s mangrove cover expanded in past decade despite prior decline, finds study
articles.summary: Mangrove vegetation along Keralam's coast expanded over the past decade despite a historical long-term decline, according to a new study by the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute. Researchers compared satellite imagery from 2017 and 2026, presenting their findings at an international symposium in Kochi on November 6, 2026, which also highlighted rising marine heatwaves in the Bay of Bengal.
articles.description: Study by ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute based in Kochi compared satellite images from 2017 and 2026 to map changes in mangrove vegetation across Keralam’s coastal districts

articles.headline: Telangana government faces financial burden to fund farmer crop compensation packages
articles.title: Telangana Govt stares at financial burden to fund Rythu Bharosa or crop compensation
articles.summary: The Telangana government faces significant financial strain as first-half revenue receipts for the 2026-27 fiscal year reached only 38.14 percent of budget projections, totaling 92,013 crore rupees. articles.description: While the date of Rythu Bharosa Yasangi installment is usually announced before December end, the announcement this time will be based on how the government plans to compensate the farmers as it had asked them not to go for Rabi cultivation in view of the ongoing El Nino

articles.headline: Imane Khelif to make professional boxing debut in Paris
articles.title: Olympic champion Imane Khelif to make professional boxing debut in December
articles.summary: Algeria’s Olympic champion Imane Khelif announced she will contest her first professional bout against Clarida Sarabia in the super-welterweight division on December 15 in Paris. articles.headline: Kurdish club Amedspor rises to second place in Turkey's Super Lig

articles.summary: Diyarbakir-based football club Amedspor has risen to second position in the Turkish Super Lig after ten matches, reflecting a changing political climate under a government peace process with the Kurdistan Workers' Party. articles.description: The Diyarbakir-based club have risen from the third tier to a top-of-the-table clash in the Turkish Super Lig.

articles.headline: Tanzanian court sentences opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years
articles.title: Tanzania court jails opposition leader for incitement, lifts treason charge
articles.summary: A Tanzanian court sentenced Chadema opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in prison for incitement following a trial that dismissed a separate treason charge. Presiding judges stated that Lissu intended to disrupt elections and instigate violence, while the politician dismissed the verdict as politically motivated orchestration directed by President Samia Suluhu Hassan's administration.
articles.description: Dismissal of treason charge means Tundu Lissu avoids threat of death penalty.

articles.headline: Protesters break into Microsoft data center construction site in Amsterdam
articles.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam
articles.summary: Demonstrators affiliated with the Geef Tegengas group breached a construction site in Amsterdam where British developer Pure Data Centres is building a facility for Microsoft. Activists scaled a crane to display banners opposing artificial intelligence and corporate involvement in geopolitics, contributing to a broader European wave of opposition against large technology infrastructure projects.
articles.description: Protesters have broken into a construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam this morning. articles.headline: Bomb threats disrupt flights across multiple European countries
articles.title: Hoax or bomb threats? What we know about flight disruptions across Europe
articles.summary: A wave of false bomb alerts disrupted flights across at least sixteen European countries, forcing authorities in Hungary and Italy to scramble fighter jets and divert aircraft. Security inspections conducted by bomb disposal teams and border police yielded no explosives, marking the second major outbreak of coordinated hoax threats affecting European aviation within a single week.
articles.description: Security inspections reveal no explosives as fighter jets escort planes amid Europe's major wave of bomb threats.

articles.headline: Macao court sentences former pro-democracy politician Au Kam-san to prison
articles.title: Macao court sentences pro-democracy ex-politician to 12.5 years in jail
articles.summary: Judicial authorities in Macao delivered a twelve-and-a-half-year prison term to sixty-nine-year-old former legislator Au Kam-san following a closed national security proceeding on Friday. The tribunal convicted the former teacher of subversion through disinformation campaigns and foreign collaboration intended to interfere with the 2024 leadership ballot. Family members condemned the verdict as politically motivated, while international human rights groups criticized the severe punishment as an intimidation tactic against peaceful dissent.
articles.description: Court finds Au Kam-san guilty of spreading false information and subversion in bid to disrupt Macao’s 2024 elections.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rejects cyber fraud bail and condemns digital criminals
articles.title: Cyber criminals have no space in society, jails only meant for them: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India declared on November 6, 2026, that cyber criminals deserve no leniency and belong strictly behind bars. Chief Justice Surya Kant emphasized that unlike some murderers, cyber fraudsters cannot be rehabilitated. The bench reviewed status reports from the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre showing a decline in digital arrest complaints across multiple states.
articles.description: A three-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant refused bail to a cyber fraud accused and did not entertain his plea to surrender after Deepavali

articles.headline: Amit Shah sets target of winning 65 seats in Uttarakhand
articles.title: Amit Shah calls for hat-trick in Uttarakhand, sets target of winning 65 seats in assembly polls
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah urged political workers during a rally in Dehradun to secure more than sixty-five constituencies in the upcoming assembly elections. Addressing the twenty-sixth Foundation Day, the minister outlined government achievements and criticized opposition leaders regarding border security and land encroachment policies ahead of the polls scheduled for early next year across the northern state.
articles.description: Addressing a public rally in Dehradun, Amit Shah asserted that the BJP is set to form the Government in Uttarakhand once again and said the “voice of Uttarakhand” should reach Rahul Gandhi

articles.headline: Lok Sabha Speaker accepts resignation of Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah
articles.title: Lok Sabha Speaker accepts Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah's resignation
articles.summary: Parliamentary authorities announced that the resignation submitted by Srinagar representative Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi has officially taken effect. The legislator previously announced his departure from both the legislative seat and the National Conference following political disagreements with the organization. This departure leaves three total vacancies within the lower house of parliament alongside existing openings in Meghalaya and West Bengal.
articles.description: Ending a bitter stalemate with the National Conference leadership, Mr. Ruhullah resigned from the Lok Sabha and the party on November 3

articles.headline: DLF and Everstone form joint venture for IREO investment
articles.title: DLF, Everstone join hands for ₹3,750-crore IREO investment
articles.summary: Real estate firm DLF Limited and investment manager Everstone Group signed an exclusive term sheet to establish a partnership targeting IREO Private Limited entities in India. The proposed collaboration involves a financial commitment of approximately three thousand seven hundred fifty crore rupees to acquire a significant economic stake. Transaction finalization is anticipated throughout the coming year under independent management oversight.
articles.description: The proposed partnership aims to unlock development potential across Delhi, Gurugram and other regions.

articles.headline: Indian-American candidates secure victories during United States midterm elections
articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners
articles.summary: Several Indian-origin candidates secured congressional victories as Democrats made gains in the United States midterm elections on November 4, 2026. Suhas Subramanyam won in Virginia and Pia Dandiya won in Florida for the House of Representatives, whereas Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy lost the Ohio gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton.
articles.description: Indian-Americans Nithya Raman won the Los Angeles mayoral race, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

articles.headline: Indian Air Force transfers sports complex land to the Centre
articles.title: IAF hands over 39.5-acre sports complex land to Centre
articles.summary: The Indian Air Force transferred 39.5 acres of land containing a sports complex and swimming pool to the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry. The handover followed notices issued by the Land and Development Office. Officials stated that a joint team will survey boundaries, while the government has recently reclaimed several prime land parcels near Lok Kalyan Marg.
articles.description: The move comes days after the Land and Development Office under the Ministry issued notices to the facility to return the land on Lok Kalyan Marg

articles.headline: Nithya Raman elected Mayor of Los Angeles after defeating incumbent Karen Bass
articles.title: Nithya Raman and her journey from Keralam to Los Angeles
articles.summary: Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass to become the Mayor of Los Angeles. Born in Keralam and raised in the United States after her family migrated, the 45-year-old Democrat previously engaged in civic activism and served on the Los Angeles City Council before winning the mayoral race.
articles.description: Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass to take charge of the second most populous city in the U.S. after New York

articles.headline: Indonesian authorities investigate alleged treason in presidential wiretapping scandal
articles.title: What to know about the presidential wiretapping scandal rocking Indonesia
articles.summary: Indonesian police have arrested chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo and two senior officers for allegedly intercepting President Prabowo Subianto's phone conversations without proper legal procedures. Authorities discovered the operation following a tip-off, suspecting it began in 2025. The high-profile arrests have heightened political tensions amid a widening rift between President Prabowo and his predecessor, Joko Widodo.
articles.description: The scandal involves senior members of President Prabowo Subianto's government, and hint at growing tensions among its elites.

articles.headline: Trump signs executive order declaring Oval Office a national monument
articles.title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Thursday designating the White House Oval Office and surrounding rooms as a national monument to protect its historic structure. The directive aims to prevent future presidents from making major architectural alterations. Legal experts criticized the move as legally meaningless while highlighting hypocrisy regarding other historic preservation laws.
articles.description: The order comes after Trump made a series of big changes to the decor of the Oval Office and tore down the White House East Wing.

articles.headline: Malaysia temporarily suspends transfer of Najib Razak to house arrest
articles.title: Court grants ex-Malaysian PM Najib house arrest after $12m royal pardon
articles.summary: Malaysia temporarily suspended the transfer of jailed former Prime Minister Najib Razak from prison to house arrest on November 6, 2026. The attorney general stated that legal questions regarding his conditional royal pardon required clarification. Najib was previously jailed for corruption linked to the 1MDB state fund, while his party had raised funds to pay a $12 million fine.
articles.description: Court had approved his transfer after the former prime minister's party paid $12m fine via crowdfunding.

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks response from NewsClick and Prabir Purkayastha on ED appeal
articles.title: Supreme Court seeks response from NewsClick, Purkayastha on ED plea against High Court order
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued notices on November 6, 2026, to news portal NewsClick and editor-in-chief Prabir Purkayastha regarding an Enforcement Directorate challenge against a Delhi High Court order. The High Court had previously quashed a money laundering case involving foreign direct investment rules, prompting the agency to seek responses within four weeks.
articles.description: At the outset, the counsel appearing for the ED submitted that they needed four weeks' time as Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, representing the agency, was not available

articles.headline: UPSC declares Civil Services Main Examination results for 2026
articles.title: UPSC Mains Result 2026 declared: Here’s how to check
articles.summary: The Union Public Service Commission announced the results of the Civil Services Main Examination on November 5, 2026. Successful candidates qualify for the personality test phase held at Dholpur House in New Delhi, which carries two hundred seventy-five marks and contributes to the final merit list alongside the written examination.
articles.description: The Civil Services exam is conducted annually in three stages - preliminary, main, and interview - to select candidates for the Indian Administrative Services (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), and Indian Police Service (IPS) and other services.

articles.headline: Court acquits five individuals in 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots mosque arson case
articles.title: Five acquitted in 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots case over mosque arson, vandalism
articles.summary: An Indian local court cleared five men of all charges relating to the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots due to insufficient evidence. Additional District and Sessions Judge Vijay Kumar delivered the verdict on November 5, 2026, following an investigation by a Special Investigation Team. The accused had faced allegations of vandalism, arson, and looting at a village mosque and a private residence during communal violence.
articles.description: According to Mr. Sharma, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) had filed a chargesheet against the five accused after investigating an incident that took place on September 8, 2013, in Muthbhar village under the Bhorakala police station limits

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu intensifies search for missing Kasimedu fishermen after Cyclone Murasu
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Search for five missing fishermen intensified, says Tamil Nadu Government
articles.summary: Authorities intensified search operations on November 6, 2026, for five missing Kasimedu fishermen following Cyclone Murasu, while opposition leaders criticised the government's response. Four bodies were previously recovered by the Indian Coast Guard after the boat suffered engine failure near Andhra Pradesh, prompting the administration to announce seven lakh rupees in initial financial relief per family.
articles.description: The nine Kasimedu fishermen who left Chennai on October 29 during Cyclone Murasu faced engine failure near Ramayapatnam Port, Andhra Pradesh, on November 3

articles.headline: Bodies of five Tamil Nadu fishermen recovered off Andhra Pradesh coast
articles.title: Bodies of five fishermen from Tamil Nadu found near Kothapatnam beach in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Indian Coast Guard officials recovered the bodies of five fishermen near the Andhra Pradesh coast following a boat capsizing incident caused by Cyclone Murasu. The vessel, carrying nine people, drifted and sank on November 3, 2026. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced a solatium of 7 lakh rupees for each family of the deceased victims.
articles.description: Indian Coast Guard staff on search for four other missing fishermen who were sailing on the same boat which sank 2 km off the shore

articles.headline: UK detains Indian ship captain over alleged Russian sanctions violations
articles.title: UK jailing of Indian sailor over Russia sanctions sets off ‘perfect storm’
articles.summary: British armed forces intercepted the crude oil tanker MT Smyrtos in the English Channel and detained Indian captain Ajay Pant for allegedly flouting Western economic restrictions against Moscow. Legal experts note this represents the first instance of a European nation keeping a commercial mariner under arrest for such offenses, potentially establishing a concerning precedent for seafarers worldwide facing prosecution.
articles.description: Captain Ajay Pant was in international waters when his allegedly 'shadow' tanker was captured by British soldiers.

articles.headline: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah denies party split after meeting legislators
articles.title: No split in National Conference, genuine issues will be addressed: Farooq Abdullah
articles.summary: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah dismissed reports of a party split on November 6, 2026, following a meeting with seventeen disgruntled legislators in Srinagar. Dr. Abdullah assured that genuine grievances regarding cabinet appointments and party demands would be addressed gradually, while reaffirming the ongoing political struggle for statehood and special constitutional status.
articles.description: ‘The baseless news of the National Conference (NC) splitting into groups is totally wrong. The party stands together. Those who think the party could be split: it was never, and it will never be split,’ says Farooq Abdullah

articles.headline: Nashra Naim elected first woman vice-president of AMU students union
articles.title: Nashra Naim elected first woman vice-president of AMU students’ union in 105-year history
articles.summary: Women secured six of the 13 posts in the Aligarh Muslim University Students Union elections, the results of which were announced on Friday, November 6, 2026. Nashra Naim became the first female vice-president in the institution's 105-year history. Mohammad Noman Ashraf won the presidency, while Mohammad Hamdan was elected secretary after elections were held following an eight-year gap.
articles.description: Women candidates won six of the 13 posts, a record five of the 10 cabinet member posts, in the first elections after an eight-year gap

articles.headline: Bihar government bans teachers and students from uploading social media reels without permission
articles.title: Bihar’s new regulations for government school teachers, non-teaching staff and students | Explained
articles.summary: The Bihar government issued new regulations on November 4, 2026, prohibiting school teachers, non-teaching staff, and students from creating or uploading social media reels without official authorization. This directive follows a formal dress code enforced on October 30, 2026, amid heightened national scrutiny regarding the condition of public educational institutions across the state.
articles.description: Under the new regulations, the State Education Department has prohibited outsiders and unauthorised persons from visiting school premises without permission from authorities

articles.headline: Jharkhand protests erupt following delayed exams and bribery allegations
articles.title: Years of delayed exams, bribery allegations provoke Jharkhand protests
articles.summary: Allegations of large-scale manipulation emerged after the results of the Jharkhand Public Service Commissions 14th Civil Services Preliminary Examination were declared in July. A controversial Optical Mark Recognition sheet circulated on messaging platforms, prompting the State government to order a Criminal Investigation Department probe, make arrests, search headquarters, and lead to the commission chairmans resignation.
articles.description: For thousands of young people across Jharkhand, the controversy was never just about one examination

articles.headline: Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flags alleged literary scam in library
articles.title: From fictitious Chief Minister to Naladiyar as ‘poet’: Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flags ‘literary scam’ in Periyar Arivulagam
articles.summary: Renowned Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flagged serious book purchase irregularities at Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore, inaugurated by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. The collection contained fictitious historical claims and authorship discrepancies. School Education Minister Rajmohan announced an immediate official government inquiry to investigate the procurement and bring those responsible to justice.
articles.description: Rajmohan, State Minister for Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, said an inquiry would be initiated immediately into the alleged scam in procurement of books at the newly inaugurated library and science centre in Tamil Nadu’s Coimbatore.

articles.headline: UNESCO adds classical Indian texts to Memory of the World regional register
articles.title: Mahabharata, Arthashastra, Rajatarangini manuscripts added to UNESCO memory regional register
articles.summary: Manuscripts of the Mahabharata, Rajatarangini, and Arthashastra were officially inscribed on the UNESCO Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register. Officials announced the milestone on November 5, 2026, following a decision made at the eleventh session held in Jakarta, Indonesia. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat praised the inclusion as a historic recognition of the nation's civilisational heritage and profound knowledge traditions.
articles.description: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat hailed the inscriptions as a landmark recognition of India’s extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage

articles.headline: Virat Kohli adopts aggressive mindset following Test cricket retirement
articles.title: Kohli 2.0 - more dangerous, feared and destructive
articles.summary: Senior international cricketer Virat Kohli has embraced a more destructive and expressive approach to white-ball batting following his retirement from Test cricket in May 2025. Observers note that India's batting depth has allowed the veteran player to shed the burdens of his past responsibilities and perform with renewed freedom during a career spanning eighteen years.
articles.description: There is a ruthless streak about him, a burning desire to stamp his dominance from the get-go; he is primed for one final shot at another 50-over World Cup winner’s medal in the Africas next year

articles.headline: Former Malaysian prime minister Najib Razak moves to house arrest
articles.title: Malaysia’s former PM Najib will serve prison time at home after paying $12.3 million for pardon
articles.summary: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak will serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest after his political party paid a 50 million ringgit fine. The payment fulfilled a key condition of a royal pardon granted by Malaysia's King. Najib has been imprisoned since August 2022 following his conviction in a corruption case linked to state fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad.
articles.description: Najib, 73, has been imprisoned since August 2022, when Malaysia’s top court upheld his conviction in a case linked to the multi-billion dollar looting of the state investment fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad

articles.headline: Automobile retail sales drop significantly in October due to high base effect
articles.title: Automobile retail sales fall 24% in October on high base effect a year ago
articles.summary: Total vehicle retail sales across India dropped 24% year-on-year to 3,172,466 units in October 2026, driven by a high base from the previous year. According to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Association, the decline was primarily optical because the previous October combined multiple major festivals. Despite the annual decrease, commercial vehicles and electric mobility segments posted strong performances during the month.
articles.description: Measured against that extraordinary base two wheelers and passenger vehicles segments faced decline

articles.headline: US judge halts construction of Trump triumphal arch in Washington
articles.title: US judge halts construction of Trump’s triumphal arch in Washington, DC
articles.summary: United States District Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered a 14-day temporary pause on the construction of President Donald Trumps proposed triumphal arch in Washington, District of Columbia. The ruling followed lawsuits filed by Vietnam War veterans concerned about the monument obstructing views between Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial after the National Capital Planning Commission approved it.
articles.description: A 14-day pause has been ordered blocking the so-called 'Arc de Trump' project in Washington, DC.

articles.headline: Lebanese citizens pack bags and stock supplies amid escalation fears
articles.title: Lebanese pack bags and stock up amid fears of new Israeli escalation
articles.summary: Residents across Lebanon are living in deep anxiety and preparing for a potential third major Israeli military escalation following previous conflicts involving the Iran-backed Shia group Hezbollah since October 2023. Families are stocking emergency supplies, keeping electronic devices charged, and packing go-bags as economic pressures rise alongside concerns over renewed regional warfare.
articles.description: Lebanese who lived through two Israeli escalations are stocking up and packing bags in case of a third.

articles.headline: Israel tightens control over Palestinian schools and revokes East Jerusalem teaching permits
articles.title: How Israel is tightening its grip on Palestinian schools in East Jerusalem
articles.summary: Palestinian teachers in occupied East Jerusalem face increasing restrictions as Israeli authorities prepare to revoke travel permits for 180 educators by the 2026-27 academic year. Meanwhile, government funding policies pressure schools to adopt the Israeli curriculum, which human rights groups warn undermines educational autonomy and replaces Palestinian history with a distorted version according to local principals.
articles.description: Israeli restrictions on teachers and pressure to adopt Israeli curriculum threaten Palestinian education in the city.

articles.headline: Indonesian police name fourth suspect in wiretapping scandal involving President Prabowo
articles.title: Indonesia names fourth wiretapping suspect as political intrigue deepens
articles.summary: Indonesian law enforcement identified a senior official with the initials SU as the fourth suspect in a high-profile wiretapping investigation targeting President Prabowo Subianto. Investigators alleged the former monitoring chief approved the interception and subsequent deletion of records. The scandal has strained political stability, intensifying tensions between President Prabowo and his predecessor Joko Widodo amid growing economic discontent.
articles.description: Scandal is driving divisions between President Prabowo Subianto and predecessor Joko Widodo.

articles.headline: Cosmoserve Space unveils India first private space debris facility
articles.title: Hyderabad startup opens India’s first private space debris recovery facility
articles.summary: Hyderabad-based startup Cosmoserve Space unveiled Base 1 on November 6, 2026, marking India’s first private space debris recovery and satellite servicing facility. Inaugurated by Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh and Telangana Minister D. Sridhar Babu, the facility features advanced laboratories for space robotics and orbital capture. Founder Dr. Chiranjeevi Phanindra stated that the company plans to conduct a full-scale debris capture demonstration by 2027 using its proprietary dual spacecraft architecture.
articles.description: Of the nearly 28,000 satellites currently in orbit, about 10,000 are non-operational, while millions of debris fragments pose risks to active satellites and space missions

articles.headline: Bhagavad Gita and Natyashastra manuscripts added to UNESCO register
articles.title: Manuscripts of Bhagavad Gita, Natyashastra inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register
articles.summary: Manuscripts of the Bhagavad Gita and Bharat Muni's Natyashastra were added to the UNESCO Memory of the World Register, bringing the total number of inscribed collections to five hundred seventy. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat described the inclusion as a historic global recognition of India's civilisational heritage, eternal wisdom, and artistic genius.
articles.description: As of April 17, 2025, 74 new documentary heritage collections were added to UNESCO’s Memory of the World Register

articles.headline: Haryana Chief Minister alleges Punjab government misallocated flood relief funds
articles.title: AAP spent Centre's ₹1,600 crore flood relief funds for Punjab elsewhere: CM Saini
articles.summary: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini alleged that the Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab misallocated sixteen hundred crore rupees provided by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for flood relief. Speaking in Chandigarh, Mr Saini claimed Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann failed to compensate farmers properly. He also criticized opposition parties for repeatedly targeting constitutional institutions and misleading citizens.
articles.description: Mr. Saini said he had earlier watched a video on social media in which Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann had promised compensation for every loss suffered by people during the devastating floods, down to a single hen.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu anti-corruption agency registers FIR in sand mining scam
articles.title: DVAC registers FIR in multi-crore sand mining case in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption registered a case and launched searches at thirty locations across Tamil Nadu following an alleged forty-seven hundred thirty crore rupee illegal sand mining scam. The Directorate of Enforcement previously flagged irregularities to the state government after experts found massive unauthorized river sand mining that generated minimal recorded revenue compared to its actual market value.
articles.description: Special teams of DVAC launched simultaneous searches at 30 locations across Tamil Nadu on November 6, 2026.

articles.headline: Indian automobile industry registers record September retail sales with thirty-two percent growth
articles.title: ‘Best ever September’: Auto retail sales surge 32% year-on-year
articles.summary: The Indian automobile sector reported 25,36,920 retail sales in September 2026, marking a 31.82 percent year-on-year increase according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Association. Five out of six vehicle categories achieved their best-ever September performance, driven by festive demand, rural cashflows, and rising electric vehicle adoption, although dealer inventory levels remained well above recommended benchmarks.
articles.description: Dealers cite festive buying in the first half of the month, steady rural and semi-urban demand, a pull towards premium motorcycles and accelerating EV adoption

articles.headline: Activist Katon Moyong rejects Arunachal Pradesh government invitation for dam talks
articles.title: Anti-dam activist rejects Arunachal government’s invitation for talks, says time for negotiations is over
articles.summary: Prominent anti-dam campaigner Katon Moyong rejected the Arunachal Pradesh government offer for discussions regarding the 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. Speaking in Itanagar on November 5, 2026, the engineer-turned-activist asserted that negotiation time had passed, alleging the initiative is politically motivated. The Adi community continues opposing the dam over displacement and heritage concerns, while officials maintain the project will drive regional economic and social growth.
articles.description: Katon Moyong, a prominent voice against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang project, called the national security argument an attempt to overcome public resistance

articles.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan accuses Keralam government of creating artificial power crisis
articles.title: Keralam power purchase row: Pinarayi accuses UDF govt of ‘creating artificial crisis’, tells CM Satheesan to disclose files
articles.summary: Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan accused the United Democratic Front administration of manufacturing an artificial electricity shortage. Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram on November 6, 2026, the politician demanded the Chief Minister release all documents concerning power purchase offers from Himachal Pradesh and GNA Energy. He alleged the administration misled the public to favor corporate monopolies, overriding standard state electricity board procedures.
articles.description: Opposition Leader accuses Chief Minister of 'openly misleading' the public with regard to power purchase deal, and thereby ‘violating’ the latter’s oath of office

articles.headline: Deepinder Goyal defends wellness wearable device Temple against criticism
articles.title: Deepinder Goyal defends ‘Temple’: ‘Not a scam; have spent over ₹188 crore to build the device’
articles.summary: Zomato co-founder Deepinder Goyal defended his health wearable device Temple on Wednesday, stating he invested thirty million dollars of his own funds into the project. Critics and doctors have raised scientific concerns regarding the device, claiming it tracks facial blood flow instead of brain activity.
articles.description: Facing growing scrutiny over his wearable device ‘Temple’, Deepinder Goyal defended the product, citing his decision to step down as Eternal CEO and invest ₹282.55 crore in its development

articles.headline: Trump blames Democratic midterm victory for stock market selloff
articles.title: Trump blames Democrats’ midterm win for U.S. stock market selloff
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump attributed Thursday's stock market decline to the Democratic Party's midterm election victories. Financial analysts indicated the selloff was driven by investor concerns that the new political majority could threaten investments in artificial intelligence data centre projects.
articles.description: Analysts attributed the fall to fears that Democrats could threaten the AI data centre investment boom, as the Nasdaq had its worst session in percentage terms since April 2025

articles.headline: US midterm voter poll highlights strong opposition to data centres
articles.title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US midterm election results?
articles.summary: A voter poll conducted for the Associated Press revealed that fifty-six percent of surveyed participants considered data centres a major factor in their voting decisions. While analysts cannot directly link opposition to specific election outcomes, key states that elected Democrats also saw increased scrutiny over artificial intelligence infrastructure.
articles.description: BBC Verify examines whether US voters were influenced by the data centre boom - and the impact anti-AI sentiment could have on the industry.

articles.headline: British families demand answers after fatal Spanish wildfires
articles.title: A wildfire killed their loved ones in Spain. These British families demand to know why
articles.summary: Relatives of British nationals killed in July wildfires in the Spanish village of Bédar expressed outrage after regional politicians blocked an official parliamentary inquiry. Families criticized authorities for failing to issue mobile phone evacuation alerts and mishandling victims' personal remains and belongings.
articles.description: Nine British nationals were among the 15 people who died when fire ripped through the village of Bédar this summer.

articles.headline: US Justice Department sues Penn State over tuition policy for undocumented students
articles.title: US Justice Department sues Penn State over undocumented students’ tuition
articles.summary: The United States Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against Pennsylvania State University alleging that its in-state tuition policy for undocumented individuals violates federal law by excluding United States citizens. According to prosecutors, the practice constitutes unlawful preferential treatment. The university stated it is reviewing the complaint, which follows similar actions nationwide.
articles.description: The lawsuit challenges Penn State's policy that allows undocumented students to qualify for reduced tuition rates.

articles.headline: India urges accountability for attacks against UN peacekeepers during debate
articles.title: Perpetrators of attacks against Blue Helmets must be held accountable: India at UN
articles.summary: Colonel Tarunendra Pratap Singh, Military Advisor at the Permanent Mission of India to the United Nations, addressed an annual debate on November 5, 2026, demanding accountability for assaults on Blue Helmets facing asymmetric threats. He emphasized that New Delhi has deployed over 300,000 troops across 50 missions and views peacekeeping as essential to global security operations.
articles.description: India is among the largest troop-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping, having deployed more than 3,00,000 troops across 50 missions to date

articles.headline: Macau court sentences former lawmaker Au Kam San to prison for subversion
articles.title: China's Macau jails ex-lawmaker in first national security trial
articles.summary: A court in Macau sentenced 69-year-old former democracy campaigner Au Kam San to 12 years and six months in prison following a closed-door trial that concluded in September 2025. He was convicted of subversion and collaborating with external organizations, becoming the first person punished under national security laws expanded in the Chinese territory in 2023.
articles.description: Au Kam San, who co-organised annual vigils for victims of the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing, is the first person convicted under national security laws widened in 2023 in Macau

articles.headline: National Payments Corporation of India establishes technology subsidiary for digital infrastructure
articles.title: NPCI sets up tech subsidiary to tap AI, blockchain, and GCC opportunities
articles.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India created a wholly owned subsidiary named NPCI Tech Solutions Limited to advance capabilities in artificial intelligence, blockchain, and digital financial infrastructure. Vishal Kanvaty was appointed as the managing director and chief executive officer of the new entity, which received approval from the Reserve Bank of India.
articles.description: NPCI Tech Solutions will focus on artificial intelligence, blockchain and digital financial infrastructure, with Vishal Kanvaty appointed as its MD and CEO

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh increases airport and port health surveillance amid Ebola concerns
articles.title: Amid rising concerns over Ebola, A.P. steps up surveillance at airports
articles.summary: The health department in Andhra Pradesh enhanced passenger screening across three airports and three ports following a video conference with federal officials on November 5, 2026. Authorities prepared isolation beds, medical equipment, and response teams across five government facilities while scheduling a mock drill for November 12 to test readiness against the expanding outbreak.
articles.description: Medical teams stationed at three airports and three ports to screen passengers arriving from Ebola-affected countries for any symptoms

articles.headline: Donald Trump signs proclamation designating Oval Office as a national monument
articles.title: Trump issues proclamation declaring Oval Office national monument
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump signed a proclamation on Thursday declaring the Oval Office and Cabinet Room as a national monument to protect the spaces from future alterations. The executive action follows his party's defeat in the midterm elections and aims to preserve the architectural integrity of areas heavily redesigned during his second term.
articles.description: Following election losses, the signing marks Trump's third event of the week focused on signature renovation projects.

articles.headline: Study finds cellophane bees produce flexible polyester that degrades in soil
articles.title: Cellophane bees produce a kind of plastic that also degrades, study finds
articles.summary: Researchers collecting translucent cell linings from ground-nesting cellophane bee nests in eastern Tennessee discovered that the material functions similarly to synthetic polyester. According to a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, testing revealed that these nest linings undergo significant degradation within months in ambient soil.
articles.description: The nest lining of the ground-nesting bee is translucent, flexible, resilient and degrades within a year

articles.headline: Milky Way grew by consuming nearby galaxies and leaving stellar streams
articles.title: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars
articles.summary: Galactic archaeologists studying stellar ages, chemical compositions, and motions discovered that the Milky Way expanded over nearly 12 billion years by devouring smaller galaxies like the Magellanic clouds. These violent collisions rip apart smaller galaxies, leaving behind distinct stellar streams that reveal the evolutionary history of our galaxy.
articles.description: Galactic archaeologists are using precise measures and larger sample sizes afforded by new missions to tease apart minute differences between groups of stars, revealing the history of the Milky Way going back almost 12 billion years

articles.headline: Democratic Socialist Nithya Raman wins LA mayoral race
articles.title: Democratic Socialist Nithya Raman wins LA mayoral race
articles.description: Nithya Raman's victory in LA marks the second major win for Democratic Socialists in a year.

articles.headline: Tanvi Patri wins silver medal at Youth Olympics in Dakar
articles.title: Tanvi Patri signs off with silver at Youth Olympics
articles.summary: Fifteen-year-old Tanvi Patri became the first Indian woman shuttler to secure an individual silver medal at the Youth Olympic Games on November 6, 2026. She lost a grueling three-game final against China's Zhang Yi Xin in Dakar. According to Badminton Association of India General Secretary Sanjay Mishra, the historic achievement reflects the immense potential of India's young sporting generation on the global stage.
articles.description: In a gripping summit clash that lasted an hour and 22 minutes, the 15-year-old Indian saved six match points and had three opportunities to seal the title

articles.headline: Building wind turbines out of parts found in Gaza’s rubble
articles.title: Building wind turbines out of parts found in Gaza’s rubble
articles.description: Palestinians in Gaza have made wind turbines to generate electricity, using scraps found in the rubble.

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh cabinet approves ₹63,296 crore greenfield corridors plan
articles.title: Madhya Pradesh cabinet approves ₹63,296 crore plan for five greenfield corridors
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh government approved a plan on November 6, 2026, to construct five greenfield expressway corridors spanning 1,398 kilometers across the state. The decision was finalized during a board meeting chaired by Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav. Officials were directed to expedite ongoing road projects to ensure that no village or city remains deprived of all-weather connectivity.
articles.description: MP is developing a modern road network through the construction of state highways, four-lane, six-lane and eight-lane roads, as well as greenfield expressways: CM Mohan Yadav

articles.headline: Kozo Tashima announces candidacy for the FIFA presidency
articles.title: Kozo Tashima: Japan leader looking to bring ‘integrity’ to FIFA
articles.summary: Kozo Tashima announced his bid to run against Gianni Infantino in the March FIFA presidential election. The 68-year-old former Japan Football Association president stated that his candidacy aims to uphold sporting integrity against commercial pressures. Tashima criticized recent decisions by football governing bodies and emphasized that the election tests FIFA ability to cleanse itself.
articles.description: The 68-year-old is set to become the first person from Japan to run for the FIFA presidency after announcing he would stand against Gianni Infantino

articles.headline: New study finds noise pollution imposes fatal stress on wildlife
articles.title: A noisy Anthropocene is imposing fatal stress on wildlife
articles.summary: A new study published in Science on November 6, 2026, revealed that extreme noise pollution in the Anthropocene negatively impacts wildlife physiologically and behaviorally. Driven by traffic, industrial activity, and sonar operations, the rising din over the past fifty years affects more than one hundred aquatic and terrestrial species worldwide, according to the paper.
articles.description: Researchers analysed over 200 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species across six continents and found that noise altered specific traits in 80% of the animals studied

articles.headline: Temple priest denies ritual rights to women in Nizamabad district
articles.title: Diktats, boycotts and the fight for rights
articles.summary: During Sri Rama Navami celebrations, a temple priest allegedly ordered women from the Goud toddy-tapper community to leave a local Ramalayam in Tallarampur village. Kairi Kalyani and her neighbors had arrived with offerings to perform rituals but faced humiliation and exclusion based on their community background. The incident highlights ongoing discrimination and the difficult fight for social rights in rural areas.
articles.description: For over two years, 45 toddy-tapper and 10 Dalit families in Nizamabad’s Tallarampur have allegedly faced a complete social boycott for defying their Village Development Committee’s (VDC) orders. Denied access to groceries, medical aid and social gatherings, they have been pushed to the margins of everyday life. The growing clout of VDCs and nearly 90 complaints of alleged excesses before the Backward Classes Commission bring the larger issue into focus, as Ravi Reddy finds during a ground visit

articles.headline: Donald Trump designates Oval Office as a national monument
articles.title: Trump designates Oval Office as national monument
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump signed an executive order on November 5, 2026, officially designating the Oval Office and Cabinet Room as national monuments to prevent future structural alterations. The announcement followed a difficult midterm election outcome for his Republican Party and drew criticism from opponents who argued the administration was ignoring pressing national concerns in favor of ongoing White House renovations.
articles.description: Critics accused Donald Trump of ignoring voter concerns over the Iran war and affordability ahead of midterm elections and obsessing instead on multiple construction and renovation projects in the capital

articles.headline: Keralam faces new challenges amid rising elderly population
articles.title: Solitary autumn years: Keralam to face new challenges with rise in elderly population
articles.summary: A domestic worker in Thiruvananthapuram named Sadia frequently travels to Tamil Nadu to care for her ailing elderly mother, spending half her salary on medical expenses while struggling with family property issues. This personal situation reflects broader socioeconomic challenges in Keralam regarding an increasing aging demographic. Published on November 6, 2026, the report highlights the growing strain on family support systems, unemployed siblings, and medical costs for elderly residents without adequate safety nets.
articles.description: Keralam’s elderly population is poised to go up significantly in a decade, which in turn, would bring up new challenges for the State in the elderly care. R.K. Roshni meets some of the elders and experts to understand the ground situation

articles.headline: White House denies departure rumours for Pete Hegseth and Marco Rubio
articles.title: White House denies Hegseth and Rubio to leave jobs after Republican election losses
articles.summary: The White House and the US State Department have rejected reports that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are leaving their posts following Republican midterm election losses. President Donald Trump expressed support for Hegseth despite criticism over the Iran war, while Rubio confirmed he plans to finish his term.
articles.description: US media reports there are calls to replace Pete Hegseth, who also faces a possible impeachment vote, while Marco Rubio is rumoured to be eyeing a presidential run.

articles.headline: Bhupender Yadav accuses Congress of spreading anarchy over electoral rolls
articles.title: Congress wants to spread anarchy in the name of democracy: Bhupender Yadav
articles.summary: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav criticized the Congress party and other opposition groups on November 5, 2026, for creating confusion regarding the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. Speaking in Patna, the Bharatiya Janata Party leader stated that the revision is a routine constitutional process managed by the Election Commission of India under Article 324.
articles.description: He added that instead of creating confusion over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the opposition should present facts to the public

articles.headline: Gaza turns discarded cooking pots into seawalls
articles.title: Gaza turns discarded cooking pots into seawalls
articles.description: As winter approaches, Palestinians in Gaza are turning damaged cooking pots into makeshift seawalls to avoid flooding.

articles.headline: Truck collision on Karra-Torpa road kills seven people in Jharkhand
articles.title: Seven including three children killed after run over by truck in Khunti
articles.summary: Seven people, including three children and three women, were killed and one person was injured after being struck by an 18-wheel truck in the Khunti district of Jharkhand. Khunti Superintendent of Police Rishabh Garg stated that the incident occurred on November 5, 2026, on the Karra-Torpa main road within the Karra police station jurisdiction.
articles.description: The incident happened on the Karra-Torpa main road within the Karra police station limits on November 5, 2026 night

articles.headline: Harmeet Kaur Dhillon resigns as United States Assistant Attorney General
articles.title: U.S. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon resigns
articles.summary: Indian-American official Harmeet Kaur Dhillon stepped down from her role leading the Department of Justice Civil Rights Division following the mid-term elections. Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the departure on Thursday on social media. Dhillon stated she delayed her public announcement per White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to ensure the news followed the conclusion of voting.
articles.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche announced her resignation in a social media post, saying Assistant Attorney General Dhillon had "led the Civil Rights Division with conviction

articles.headline: West Bengal government discusses Ashok Leyland plant for Singur site
articles.title: Will do something for Singur, West Bengal CM signals fresh industrial push
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced on November 5, 2026, that his administration is in discussions with Ashok Leyland to establish a vehicle manufacturing plant in Singur. Speaking during the unveiling of the state investment promotion policy, Adhikari outlined plans to purchase land directly through state funds without utilizing police force for acquisitions.
articles.description: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the government was in talks with Ashok Leyland for setting up a plant at Singur

articles.headline: Union Minister J.P. Nadda sets March 2027 completion deadline for AIIMS Awantipora
articles.title: J&K’s health sector receives a shot in arm as Union Minister J.P. Nadda sets AIIMS deadline for March
articles.summary: Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda announced on November 5, 2026, that the All India Institute of Medical Sciences in Awantipora will be completed by March 2027. During a project review, Nadda directed officials to prioritize essential equipment procurement to facilitate outpatient department services and prepare for the commencement of MBBS classes in 2027.
articles.description: During a review of the phase-wise construction and handover plan, the Union Minister was informed that Phase-I buildings, including the OPD Registration Block, OPD Block, residential buildings and designated hostels, had been completed

articles.headline: Violence disrupts third phase of Rajasthan panchayat elections
articles.title: Violence mars third phase of Rajasthan panchayat elections
articles.summary: Clashes, stone-pelting, and allegations of bogus voting marred the third phase of panchayat elections across twenty-seven districts of Rajasthan on Thursday. Supporters of rival candidates fought in multiple districts, resulting in one death and several injuries in Jhunjhunu district. Police detained suspects and utilized a lathi charge to control crowds, while voting was cancelled at one village panchayat due to a missing candidate.

articles.headline: Kanchan Katkar crafts silver ornaments in Hupari for decades
articles.title: The silver hands of Hupari
articles.summary: Residing within the twisting lanes of Hupari town, seventy-six-year-old Kanchan Katkar meticulously attaches silver ghungroos to chain loops using iron tongs. Having completed school in 1970, she chose to remain single following the marriage of her sisters in order to care for her parents, who had actively participated in the Indian freedom struggle.
articles.description: In Maharashtra’s Hupari town, women artisans drive a ₹1,000-crore silver industry, sustaining a century-old trade. Radheshyam Jadhav reports on how, despite being underpaid and excluded from formal leadership, they forge their own economic autonomy in a deeply traditional landscape

articles.headline: OpenAI drops non-disclosure agreements for upcoming data center community projects
articles.title: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
articles.summary: Following recent midterms where voters opposed data center expansions, OpenAI announced it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials for future projects. The ChatGPT maker promised to cover full electricity and infrastructure costs, publish job creation data, and establish local compacts reflecting community priorities in regions where it operates compute campuses.
articles.description: Following this week's midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won't use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials. Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions […]

articles.title: Israeli settlers set fire to Palestinian olive grove near Ramallah
articles.description: Israeli settlers have set fire to olive trees belonging to Palestinian farmers in the village of Burqa, near Ramallah.

articles.headline: Airbnb develops artificial intelligence travel agent for 2027 release
articles.title: Airbnb is working on an AI travel agent
articles.summary: Airbnb plans to launch an artificial intelligence agent in the first half of 2027 to assist users with trip planning and bookings, according to its third-quarter shareholder letter. Chief Executive Officer Brian Chesky stated that the custom-designed interface will dynamically compose elements like maps and itineraries rather than operating as a traditional chatbot.
articles.description: Airbnb plans to roll out an AI agent in the first half of 2027 that will help users plan and book travel, the company said in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter released today. articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV begins Latin American tour following lung cancer surgery
articles.title: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV is embarking on a twelve-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru just three weeks after undergoing surgery to remove a lung tumor. The Vatican stated that no extraordinary health measures are required for the seventy-one-year-old pontiff, whose itinerary features a homecoming to Peru where he previously served as a priest.
articles.description: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

articles.headline: Kashmir faces ongoing terror threats despite drop in local militants
articles.title: Just one local terrorist active in Kashmir, but terror threat remains: IGP Sujit Kumar
articles.summary: Inspector General of Police Sujit Kumar reported that militancy in Kashmir has dropped to one active local terrorist, identified as Lateef Ahmad, alongside transitioning foreign operatives. Speaking on November 5, 2026, the official noted that security forces remain on alert while addressing additional regional challenges involving drug abuse, cybercrime, and traffic violations.
articles.description: The police identified Lateef Ahmad, 21, a resident of south Kashmir’s Kulgam, as the terrorist behind the Anantnag attack, which left one policeman dead in Anantnag’s Lal Chowk

articles.headline: Delhi implements winter action plan to combat seasonal air pollution
articles.title: Delhi's toxic winter air is back - is the Indian capital prepared for pollution?
articles.summary: The Delhi government has launched a Winter Action Plan to address the city's annual spike in toxic air pollution. The measures include construction bans and vehicle restrictions effective through February. While experts welcome the early planning, they warn that long-term success depends on stricter enforcement and regional cooperation to address diverse sources of harmful emissions.
articles.description: The Delhi government has announced a four-month winter action plan, but experts say that won't be enough.

articles.headline: Perplexity launches new work-focused AI agents
articles.title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence startup Perplexity has introduced always-on workspace agents called Teammates to compete with offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic. Operating continuously, these agents integrate with Perplexity Computer to handle concurrent large-scale tasks. The feature is available exclusively through the platform's two hundred dollars per month Max subscription plan, allowing users to monitor progress via dedicated application threads and Slack integrations.
articles.description: Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup's new always-on "Teammates" can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use. Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer, an AI system that can deploy agents on your device […]
